name: Nationalist Congress Party
description: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) is an Indian political party founded in 1999 by Sharad Pawar, P. A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar after separating from the Indian National Congress. The party has its main base in Maharashtra and follows principles of democracy, secularism, social justice, federalism and economic development. NCP has played an important role in Maharashtra politics and has participated in coalition governments at both state and national levels.
currentLeader: Ajit Pawar (NCP faction) / Sharad Pawar (NCP-SP faction)
alliance: Varies by faction; NCP (Ajit Pawar) aligned with NDA, NCP (Sharad Pawar) aligned with INDIA Alliance
achievements: Played a major role in Maharashtra coalition governments.
Sharad Pawar served multiple terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra before founding NCP.
Supported development of agriculture and cooperative institutions in Maharashtra.
Held important Union government portfolios including Agriculture.
Contributed to expansion of cooperative banking and sugar industries in Maharashtra.
Participated in the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government from 2004 to 2014.
Worked on policies related to farmers, rural development and food security.
Maintained influence in Maharashtra's political landscape for decades.
criticisms: Opposition parties have accused NCP leaders of corruption and misuse of power.
The party has faced criticism over family-based leadership structure.
The 2023 split between Sharad Pawar and Ajit Pawar factions created internal conflicts.
Critics have questioned frequent alliance changes by party leaders.
Opponents have raised concerns regarding influence of cooperative sector politics.
protests: Campaigns supporting farmers' rights and agricultural reforms.
Protests regarding unemployment and economic issues.
Campaigns for federal rights of states.
Demonstrations on issues affecting Maharashtra farmers.
timeline: 1999 - Nationalist Congress Party founded by Sharad Pawar, P. A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar.
1999 - NCP formed alliance with Congress in Maharashtra and joined state government.
2004 - NCP became part of the UPA alliance at the national level.
2009 - NCP continued participation in UPA government.
2014 - NCP contested Maharashtra Assembly elections independently.
2019 - NCP, Congress and Shiv Sena formed the Maha Vikas Aghadi government in Maharashtra.
2021 - Sharad Pawar remained a key opposition leader nationally.
2023 - Ajit Pawar split from Sharad Pawar and joined the Maharashtra government.
2024 - NCP factions contested Lok Sabha elections under different alliances.

statesGoverned.status: Participated in coalition governments multiple times (1999–2014, 2019–2022)
